sections.content: Tanto... como (both... and, as much... as) links two elements as equally necessary or equally true, the natural tool for a closing synthesis that wants to name several factors as jointly essential rather than ranking one above the other. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Tanto la concentración extrema de la tierra como la existencia de un movimiento obrero organizado resultan condiciones casi siempre presentes.
items.english: Both extreme land concentration and the existence of an organized labor movement turn out to be conditions almost always present.

items.spanish: Tanto los países con enorme desigualdad de tierra como los países con fuertes movimientos sindicales experimentaron décadas de tensión.
items.english: Both countries with enormous land inequality and countries with strong union movements experienced decades of tension.

items.spanish: Lo que distingue un país donde estalla una revolución es tanto la debilidad del Estado como la capacidad de las fuerzas de oposición para actuar coordinadamente.
items.english: What distinguishes a country where a revolution breaks out is both the weakness of the state and the opposition forces' ability to act in a coordinated way.

items.spanish: Con estas herramientas conceptuales -tanto la definición de revolución como sus precondiciones estructurales- estamos ya preparados para examinar el caso mexicano.
items.english: With these conceptual tools -- both the definition of revolution and its structural preconditions -- we are now ready to examine the Mexican case.

sections.content: Tanto stays invariable here (never tanta/tantos/tantas) because it isn't quantifying a noun by itself -- it's the fixed first half of the tanto... como pair, whatever gender or number the nouns that follow happen to have.
